# Saginaw Bay Report

> Live Saginaw Bay fishing conditions built on wind direction. Which shore is in the lee, which shore has the
> stacked water, and whether it is worth launching. Built and maintained by Chris Izworski in Bay City.

## Three zones, not one fishery
Inner Bay is protected shallow water a small boat can fish. Lower Bay is open water 18 to 35 feet where the
trophy walleye live and where there is no shelter at all. Eastern Bay is shallow and weedy with perch and pike
in the mix. Each has its own page, its own depths, and its own launches.

## What makes this different
Most fishing condition tools publish a solunar or barometric "bite score" that is identical for every water in
the country. On Saginaw Bay the governing variable is wind, because the bay is over a thousand square miles and
almost none of it is deep. This site computes two answers from live buoy wind and the bay's geometry: the lee
shore, where you can launch and stay comfortable, and the windward shore, where water and bait stack up and
walleye tend to concentrate. Those are usually opposite shores, and choosing between them is the real decision.

## Pages, all one click from the front page
- [Live conditions](https://saginawbay.chrisizworski.com/)
- [Wind and fish location](https://saginawbay.chrisizworski.com/wind-and-fish-location.html): the cornerstone guide
- [Walleye](https://saginawbay.chrisizworski.com/walleye.html): spring run through the fall bite
- [Perch](https://saginawbay.chrisizworski.com/perch.html)
- [Inner Bay](https://saginawbay.chrisizworski.com/inner-bay.html): Bay City, Linwood, Pinconning, 8 to 17 feet
- [Lower Bay](https://saginawbay.chrisizworski.com/lower-bay.html): Thomas Road, Finn Road, Callahan Reef, 18 to 35 feet
- [Eastern Bay](https://saginawbay.chrisizworski.com/eastern-bay.html): Sebewaing, Wildfowl Bay, Fish Point, 8 to 20 feet
- [Saginaw River](https://saginawbay.chrisizworski.com/saginaw-river.html)
- [Launches and access](https://saginawbay.chrisizworski.com/launches-and-access.html)

## Data sources
- NOAA NDBC buoys SBLM4 (Saginaw Bay Light, inner bay), GSLM4 (Gravelly Shoal Light), TAWM4 (Tawas Point)
- USGS gauges 04157005 (Saginaw River at Saginaw) and 04157060 (Bay City): discharge, stage, water temperature,
  and turbidity. The gauge chain runs down the river with decreasing lag to the bay, so turbidity upstream is a
  preview of bay water colour roughly half a day out
- NOAA CO-OPS station 9075014 at Harbor Beach for Lake Huron water level against the long term mean
- National Weather Service API
- Michigan DNR for seasons, limits and regulations, which are never restated here

## Honesty notes
Shore reads are geometry plus weather, not a prediction that fish will bite. The launch read is built from wind
speed and fetch and cannot know your hull. Buoy observations older than three hours are flagged stale rather
than shown as current; the outer bay buoy is frequently offline outside the shipping season. Ice conditions are
not covered here, they live at the Michigan Ice Report.
